title: Sound & microphone
blurb: No sound, wrong speaker, crackling, microphone not picking up.

remedies.title: No sound from the computer
remedies.why: Sound goes to another device (a monitor, headset or TV), is muted, or the audio service stopped.

steps.text: Check the volume and mute, including the keys on the keyboard and any speaker knobs.
Pick the right output: click the speaker in the taskbar › the arrow next to the volume › choose the speaker or headset.
Pick the right output in Sound › Output (monitors and TVs often grab the sound).
Restart the Windows audio service.
Check the app's own volume in the mixer.
Unplug headphones and Bluetooth devices, then try the built-in speakers.
Restart the Mac if sound stays missing; that restarts the sound system.

remedies.title: Sound plays through the wrong speaker or headset
remedies.why: The system switched to a newly connected device (a monitor, dock or Bluetooth headset).

steps.text: Choose the output in Settings › System › Sound › Output, and set it as default in More sound settings.
Choose the output in Sound › Output; hold Option and click the menu-bar speaker to switch quickly.
In meeting apps set the speaker in the app too; they don't always follow the system.
Disable devices you never use (like a monitor's speakers) so they stop taking over: Sound control panel › right-click › Disable.

remedies.title: Sound crackles, pops or stutters
remedies.why: The computer is overloaded, audio enhancements misbehave, a USB/Bluetooth link is weak, or the sound driver is old.

steps.text: Close heavy apps and see if it stops.
Turn off audio enhancements: Settings › Sound › your speaker › Audio enhancements: Off.
Set a lower format (24-bit 48000 Hz) under the speaker's Properties › Advanced.
In Audio MIDI Setup set the output to 48,000 Hz.
For USB headsets, plug straight into the computer instead of a hub or dock.
Update the sound driver (Windows Update › Optional updates, or the PC maker's site).

remedies.title: Microphone doesn't pick anything up
remedies.why: Privacy settings block apps, the wrong microphone is selected, or the input level is very low or muted.

steps.text: Allow microphone access for apps and desktop apps.
Allow each app in Privacy & Security › Microphone.
Choose the microphone in Sound › Input and raise its volume; speak and watch the level move.
Choose the microphone in Sound › Input and raise the input volume.
Check for a mute switch on the headset or its cable.
Restart the Windows audio service.

remedies.title: My microphone is too quiet or too loud
remedies.why: The input level is set low, or the app adjusts it automatically.

steps.text: Raise the input volume (Windows also has Microphone Boost under Sound control panel › Recording › Properties › Levels).
Raise the input volume in Sound › Input.
In Teams/Zoom turn off automatic microphone adjustment if it keeps changing.
Move the microphone closer (2–3 finger widths from your mouth for a headset).

remedies.title: Plugged-in headphones don't work
remedies.why: The plug isn't fully in, the computer doesn't detect it, or a headset with one plug is in a headphone-only port.

steps.text: Push the plug in firmly; cases on phones and some laptops stop it seating.
Pick the headphones as the output in Sound settings.
Pick the headphones as the output in Sound settings.
Try another pair; if it works, the first pair is faulty.
Look for dust in the jack and blow it out gently.

remedies.title: Volume keys or mute key don't work
remedies.why: The function keys are set to F1–F12 mode, or the keyboard's helper software isn't running.

steps.text: Hold Fn while pressing the key, or press Fn+Esc (many laptops) to switch the function-key mode.
Change "Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys" in Keyboard settings › Keyboard Shortcuts › Function Keys.
Reinstall the laptop maker's hotkey app (often in its support tools).

remedies.title: No sound from the TV or monitor over HDMI
remedies.why: Sound still goes to the laptop's speakers, or the TV/monitor's own volume is muted.

steps.text: Choose the TV or monitor as the output.
Choose the TV or monitor as the output.
Turn up the TV or monitor's own volume, and check its audio input setting.
Some adapters (especially cheap USB-C to HDMI) don't carry sound; try another.
